About the screenshots

These were taken from a real AW1000 running this firmware. The status page is LuCI's own: the theme draws its tables as boxes, and no part of it is patched by this repository.

docs.title: The settings page: System → Footstrap
docs.text:
The theme registers one page of its own, System → Footstrap, with four tabs: Colour scheme, Interface, Background and Colours.

Changes there apply to the browser you are in immediately. Three buttons decide what happens next:

  • Save to router writes the look into /etc/config/footstrap, so every other browser and device that opens the page gets it too. A browser that has chosen its own look keeps that choice.
  • Reset to router drops this browser's own changes and follows the router again.
  • Reset to built-in goes back to the defaults the theme itself ships with.

docs.title: The look a new router starts with
docs.text:
A fresh install does not start at the theme's own defaults: files/etc/uci-defaults/50-cw-footstrap-look writes the image's default look into /etc/config/footstrap on first boot - dark mode, the top layout, the Footstrap palette, 12 px rounding, frosted surfaces - together with the two files that make up its background:

  • files/etc/footstrap/login-bg, the photo behind the pages and the login card;
  • files/etc/footstrap/pattern.svg, the pattern the pattern wallpaper mode draws.

The two settings that name those files hold their checksums, so the script reads the checksums off the files actually installed rather than trusting a number written down. It runs once: it marks the look it applied, and a router whose look has already been saved to the router is left alone - your choice always outranks the image's.

docs.title: Switching themes
docs.text:
Footstrap is selected on the first boot. To change it later:

System → System → Language and Style → Design

The stock Bootstrap theme stays installed as the fallback. Argon and Alpha are in the image as well, each its own package with its own licence and pin, so the three can be compared on the device. Alpha is written for an older LuCI layout, so if choosing it leaves pages that do not look right, that is what you are seeing - nothing else about the firmware changes when you switch.

docs.title: Notes for developers
docs.text:
The theme installs its ucode templates under /usr/share/ucode/luci/template/themes/footstrap/ (header.ut, footer.ut, sysauth.ut and two partials), its resources under /www/luci-static/footstrap/, its settings view at /usr/share/luci/menu.d/luci-theme-footstrap.json pointing at footstrap/appearance, and its own /etc/config/footstrap conffile with a first-boot script of its own. Because that conffile belongs to the package, this repository ships no copy of it: the image's look is applied by the uci-defaults script above instead.

The two background files live in /etc/footstrap/, which the theme's own /lib/upgrade/keep.d/luci-theme-footstrap lists, so a sysupgrade keeps whatever the admin uploaded there. /www/luci-static/footstrap/bg and .../fonts are symlinks into that directory.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Does CleanWRT have a dark mode?

Yes, and it is the default. System → Footstrap → Colour scheme → Mode offers Auto (follows your system), Light and Dark; a browser can also keep its own choice, which Reset to router gives up.

Does the theme work on a phone?

Yes. The layout collapses below 768 px, and the density and content width are adjustable on the settings page.

How do I switch back to the default OpenWrt theme?

Go to System → System → Language and Style → Design and pick Bootstrap. Bootstrap stays installed in the image precisely so that this is always possible.

Does CleanWRT patch the theme?

One line, for branding: the login page shows the CleanWRT logo instead of the router's hostname. Everything else is the upstream package at its pinned commit. The logo is this repository's own file (files/www/luci-static/cw-branding/login-logo.png), outside the theme's directory, so a theme update can neither overwrite it nor collide with the patch. The look a new router starts with is added by a first-boot script and two background files, not by a patch.

docs.title: UART guide
docs.text: The serial console (UART) is how you reach the bootloader. It is required for the first install from the stock firmware, and it is the universal recovery path as long as the bootloader is intact.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text: Item Notes USB-UART adapter 3.3 V logic only. A 5 V adapter can damage the board. Three jumper wires TX, RX and GND. Do not connect the adapter's power pin. Phillips screwdriver to open the case Terminal program screen, minicom, PuTTY or similar

docs.title: Connection settings
docs.text: Setting Value Speed 115200 baud Data / parity / stop 8N1 Flow control none

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text:
Locate the UART pads on the board. They are marked for TX, RX and GND.

  • Router TX to adapter RX
  • Router RX to adapter TX
  • Router GND to adapter GND

Cross the data lines: transmit goes to receive. If you see nothing, swap TX and RX before you suspect anything else.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
# Linux
screen /dev/ttyUSB0 115200
# macOS
screen /dev/tty.usbserial-XXXX 115200

Power the router on. You should see the boot messages. To stop the boot at the bootloader, press a key when the countdown appears. You are now at the U-Boot prompt, and the installation and recovery steps can continue from there.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Disconnect the adapter's power wire; the router must power itself.
  • Keep the serial session open while you flash; it shows exactly what failed if something does.
  • Close the terminal when you are done. A stuck terminal on the modem's AT port (not the board UART) is a different matter, see The 5G modem.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
What UART settings does the Arcadyan AW1000 use?

115200 baud, 8N1, no flow control, at 3.3 V logic. Connect router TX to adapter RX, router RX to adapter TX and ground to ground, and leave the adapter's power pin unconnected.

Can I use a 5 V serial adapter on the AW1000?

No. Use 3.3 V logic only. A 5 V adapter can damage the board.

I see nothing on the AW1000 serial console. What should I check?

Swap the TX and RX wires first, since the data lines must cross. Then check that the grounds are joined, that the speed is 115200, and that you open the terminal before you power the router on.

How do I stop U-Boot on the AW1000?

Power the router on with the serial terminal open and press a key when the countdown appears. You are then at the U-Boot prompt, ready for the installation or recovery steps.

docs.title: Firmware updates
docs.text: Install a new release with sysupgrade (see Installation). Keep settings between CleanWRT releases; use a clean install (-n) when changing major versions or when a release note asks for it.

docs.title: What is pinned, and why
docs.text:
An on-device apk upgrade once replaced the LuCI pages with the upstream builds and silently dropped the project's patches (the overview cards went back to plain tables). To prevent that, the following are pinned to the versions of the release:

Pinned Because every package from the LuCI feed the patched pages must never be replaced by a stock build base-files its files in /rom are read-only the kernel and every kmod-* they are tied to the running kernel; a kernel change is always a flash

They change only with the next firmware release.

Every other package is unpinned. apk update && apk upgrade delivers upstream security fixes (for example openssl, mbedtls, ca-bundle, uhttpd).

Upgrading packages restarts services

Upgrading packages restarts the affected services (network, Wi-Fi, web server) for a moment.

docs.title: If a package upgrade breaks something
docs.text: Recovery from a failed package upgrade is flashing the release again. A factory reset does not restore packages that were replaced.

docs.title: Pins are renewed after every flash
docs.text: The pin list is generated from the installed package database on the first boot after a flash, including a keep-settings sysupgrade. The pins therefore always match the running image, and an old pin can never demand a downgrade.

docs.title: Source pins in the repository
docs.text: For builders: every feed is pinned to a commit in feeds.conf.default, and the packages that are not feeds are pinned in configs/local-packages.pin. The build fails if a checkout does not match its pin. See Build from source.

docs.title: What is new
docs.text:
The changelog is the record of what shipped. This page is the same history read the other way round: what changes for you if you are on the release before.

Which release am I on?

cat /etc/openwrt_release
The LuCI login footer shows the same string. The version is also the first line of the Health tab's log view.

docs.title: Calls
docs.text: The Calls tab is the line's memory: every call the router handled, in one list, newest first, with whatever that call left behind attached to it.

docs.title: What one call record holds
docs.text:
field what it says type IN an incoming call, OUT one you placed, MISS a call that rang and was not taken number the digits the network sent, shown in the form your numbering plan says. A contact's name from the phone book replaces it when the digits match time when the call was decided, from the router's clock duration seconds of connected call. A missed call has none outcome one word: see below cause the reason behind the outcome when there is one to give answered by only when someone took it: handset, machine, web or sip recording the file this call was recorded to, when recording was on message the answering-machine message this call left, when it did outcome what happened answered the call was taken and connected missed it rang and nobody answered. The network ended it no_answer the call was never answered from this side, recorded separately from a plain miss rejected you refused it — the handset's code, the page's Reject, or a quiet-hours window set to release callers blocked a rule stopped it before it rang busy the line was engaged failed the attempt did not get through: no service, the modem refused the dial, or the network released it

What the log never holds

A name is not stored, only the digits and, at display time, the phone-book entry they match. A recording or message file name never contains a phone number — a file is named for the call's time and its id, so a leaked file is not a leaked contact list. The service log (logread) carries no numbers either; the display form of a number is a property of the page.

docs.title: Reading the list
docs.text:
The tab carries the line's state at the top and the list below it.

control what it does the search box matches digits or a contact name as you type the filter chips All, Outgoing, Incoming, Missed, Answered, Blocked. The last two are views on the outcome, not kinds of call, and each chip carries its count From date limits the list to calls from that date on Export CSV the list as it currently stands, filters included: Type, Number, Name, Date, Duration (s), Result, Answered by, Network cause Clear all empties the log. It is disabled while a result filter is showing, because the daemon deletes by call type a call's own card opens under the row: the fields above, and the audio controls for whatever this call left behind

A card's audio controls are play, save and delete, and they appear only when that call actually has something to play — a call with no recording and no message shows nothing extra. The card also offers Add to phone book, and Block incoming / Block outgoing for that number, which are absent when the caller withheld their number.

docs.title: Where the log lives
docs.text:
Two copies, deliberately:

path what it is /var/run/awvoice-phoned/calls.json the working copy, in memory-backed storage, so a call that ends does not write to flash /etc/awvoice/calls.json the copy on flash, which is what survives a reboot

The daemon flushes its in-memory log when it stops, so the two agree after a clean restart. If the flash copy is ever unreadable — a cut write, a hand edit with a stray character — the daemon renames it to calls.json.bad rather than overwrite it, and starts a fresh log. Your old records are still in that file.

Both copies are kept across a sysupgrade, because the package ships a keep-list entry for /etc/awvoice/. See files and ports.

Two limits worth knowing: the log holds the most recent 200 calls and drops the 201st, and the memory copy is written down to flash at most every ten minutes, so a power cut can lose the last few minutes of records. The flash copy is written as a temporary file and renamed, mode 0600, so it is never half-written.

docs.title: The outcome words in real life
docs.text: you want to know read who rang while you were out type MISS, and the time whether the answering machine took a call answered by machine, and the message attached to that row whether the browser page answered answered by web whether a soft phone answered answered by sip why a call you placed failed outcome failed and the cause whether a rule stopped a caller outcome blocked — the rule that matched is on the Rules tab whether quiet hours held a call quiet outcome plus the cause word, and the Health tab says what decided the last call

docs.title: Settings on this page
docs.text:
The log itself has no options. What changes what appears in it:

option default effect on the log record_enabled 0 with it on, each answered call carries a recording machine_enabled 0 with it on, unanswered calls carry a message and are marked answered by the machine region auto the form a number is displayed in. The stored digits do not change phone-book entries none a matching number is shown as its contact name

docs.title: When the list looks wrong
docs.text: symptom what it means The list is empty after calls were made the page reads the daemon, so an empty list with a running daemon means the flash copy was unreadable and a new log started. Look for /etc/awvoice/calls.json.bad Calls are there but no recordings recording is off by default. It records what it hears from the moment it is switched on, not the calls before A recording is missing from an old call recordings are attached after the fact: the log line and the file are separate, and a file deleted by the size budget leaves the call without one Names show as numbers the phone-book entry does not match the digits the network sent. The rules page explains how a number is matched Times are wrong the router's clock. Set your time zone; the log stores the moment, the page shows it in the browser's zone

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
Does CleanWRT keep a record of every call?

Yes, in the call log: type, number, time, duration and outcome for every call the router handled. It is stored on the router under /etc/awvoice/ and survives an upgrade that keeps settings. Nothing is sent anywhere.

Are call recordings kept on the router or somewhere else?

On the router only, as WAV files in /etc/awvoice/recordings/. There is no upload, no remote storage and no network share involved. Play, save or delete them from the call's own card.

Can I export the call log?

The Calls tab exports what it is currently showing as CSV, filters included.

Does the log show who answered — the handset or the page?

Yes. A call someone took carries answered by: handset, machine, web or sip.

docs.title: The handset
docs.text: This page is the line as an ordinary telephone behaves: what you hear, what the keys do, and what the settings behind each behaviour are. The browser's own phone is a separate page, and what happens when nobody answers is the answering machine.

docs.title: The states the line reports
docs.text:
The page's Overview tab shows one word for the line, and every other control follows from it.

state what it means Idle the handset is on the hook and the line is ready. A dial tone is available Handset lifted off hook: the line is open, dialling is accepted, nothing is connected yet Ringing an incoming call is announcing itself to the handset In call a call is up, and the audio path is carrying it No service the modem is not registered, so the line cannot be used until it is Phone service down the daemon is not running. The line chip is in reset, so the phone cannot ring

A dead service is a silent line, by design

When awvoice-phoned stops, the kernel module's watchdog puts the line chip back into reset within milliseconds. A phone that keeps ringing after its daemon dies is the failure this prevents. See how it works.

docs.title: Tones
docs.text:
Dial tone while off hook and idle, ringing tone toward the caller you are dialing, busy and congestion at the ends of a failed attempt. What you hear while waiting for a answered call is decided by one option:

ringback what you hear before the other side answers auto (default) the router's own progress tone until the network's audio arrives, then the network's on the local tone, always off nothing until the call is answered

Tone levels and the modem's receive gain are settings on the Settings tab; two of them, earpiece_volume and modem_rx_gain, are written to the modem only when you set them, and are unset out of the box.

docs.title: Dialling
docs.text:
Digits are collected while you dial and released to the network when the number ends. A number ends on a pause: dial_pause_s, between 3 and 15 seconds, 6 by default. A handset that sends digits slowly needs the longer end of that range; a fast keypad can go shorter.

Three-digit service codes need a longer hook break than a flash. The two windows are separate on purpose: the handset's flash window (flash_min_ms 80 to flash_max_ms 300 by default) decides what counts as a flash, and a code typed inside the window that follows it is read as a code, not as a digit. That is why a flash followed by 3 joins two calls and a long hook break followed by a service code reaches the network.

A hotline number goes out by itself when the handset is lifted: set the number, and hotline_delay_s (10 by default) is the window in which you can still dial somewhere else.

docs.title: Hook-flash codes
docs.text:
Press the handset's flash (R) key during a call, then one digit:

after the flash what happens 1 end the current call and take the other one — the waiting call, or the held one 2 put the current call on hold and take the other; with two live calls this swaps them, with one held call it takes it back 0 refuse the waiting call, or release the held one 3 join the two calls into one three-way conversation. Needs two calls up and 3-way calling switched on in Phone settings, which it is not as installed

The same codes are on the browser page's Flash button, which is the handset's flash key in the same slot.

Refusing a second call while it still rings

Giving up a ringing second call ends every call on the line. The modem cannot release a ringing leg on its own, so the network releases the dialog. Take the call first, then hang up.

docs.title: Call waiting, hold and three-way
docs.text:
call_waiting is on by default. A second call is announced during a call — a 500 ms tone every five seconds — and you can hold the first call and take the second, swap between them, or refuse the newcomer. With call_waiting off the second call is refused on arrival.

The three-way join is a separate switch: conference, off as installed. A flash and 3 with it off does nothing but log three-way calling is off, so the key is not lost, it is declined. Turn it on in Phone settings → Features → 3-way calling if you want it.

docs.title: Recall
docs.text:
Put the handset down while a call is on hold and the call is not lost: the phone rings back until you lift it, which takes the call back, or the other side ends it.

This is also the rule that decides who owns a call the browser page put on hold. A lift during a page call carries the call on at the handset — the log records the handset as the one that answered it, and the page's microphone and speaker stop with it. A call the page held is not taken by a lift: the lift gets the recall dial tone and the held call stays the page's.

docs.title: Caller id
docs.text:
The number and name are sent to the handset's display as a message on the line. Two settings decide it, and both are visible on the Settings tab:

cid the signalling the handset expects dtmf (default) the DTMF variant, which most cheap handsets understand bellcore FSK, Bellcore framing etsi FSK, ETSI framing off nothing is sent cid_when where the message sits relative to the first ring ring1 (default) after the first ring prering in the gap before it, which some handsets need and some networks ignore

cid_when matters only for the two FSK modes. With cid on the DTMF variant the message goes out while the phone is ringing, and the page shows the timing control disabled, because there is nothing for it to decide.

A caller-id message carries digits only. How those digits are displayed — national form, international form, with or without the name from your phone book — is decided by the numbering plan, region: auto (default) follows the network the line registers on, across 43 regions, or you can name one. The number the network sent is never rewritten; the plan decides the shape it is shown in.

Nothing appears on the handset display

Check cid first: a handset that expects FSK shows nothing when the router sends the DTMF variant, and the other way round. Then check cid_when. The Tools tab can transmit a caller-id message on demand, which tells you whether the line is sending it at all.

docs.title: The numbers you do not show
docs.text:
Calling-line restriction (CLIR) hides your number on the calls you place: clir takes network (the default, which asks nothing), hide or show, and maps to AT+CLIR=0|1|2. It has no control on the page — it is set in /etc/config/awvoice, and saving the page leaves whatever is stored there untouched. The Health tab reports what the network provisioned, as not_provisioned, provisioned, unknown, restricted or allowed, so a restriction that the operator will not carry is visible rather than assumed.

Network service codes are dialled as you would dial them on any phone. A prefix of #31# or *31# on a dialled number is understood as a per-call restriction request and is stripped before any blocking rule looks at the number.

my_number is a display-only setting. Whatever you put there appears on the page so you know which number this line is; nothing is ever dialled from it.

docs.title: The phone LED
docs.text:
The front-panel phone LED follows the line, and one option names it: led, which ships as green:phone. Set it to an empty value and the LED is left alone entirely.

the line the LED ready solid a call is ringing fast blink — ring_rate_ms, 300 by default the handset is off hook slow blink — offhook_rate_ms, 1000 by default

The other five lamps on the panel belong to LED Management, which does not touch this one while AWvoice is running.

docs.title: Settings on this page
docs.text:
option (awvoice.main) values default the page calls it dial_pause_s 3–15 6 Dial pause flash_min_ms / flash_max_ms 20–500 / 300–3000 80 / 300 Flash window call_waiting 0 | 1 1 Call waiting conference 0 | 1 0 3-way calling cid dtmf | bellcore | etsi | off dtmf Caller id mode cid_when ring1 | prering ring1 Caller id timing ringback auto | on | off auto Ringback region auto | a region name auto Numbering plan hotline_delay_s seconds 10 Hotline delay led an LED name, or '' green:phone Phone LED ring_rate_ms milliseconds 300 Ring blink rate offhook_rate_ms milliseconds 1000 Off-hook blink rate my_number digits unset My number

flash_max_ms must be at least 100 ms above flash_min_ms; the page refuses a pair that is not. The full option list, including the ones the page does not show, is in the settings reference.

docs.title: When it misbehaves
docs.text: symptom the one check that decides it No dial tone with the handset lifted is the service running and the modem registered? The Overview word tells you which of the two it is Digits are cut off, or the call dials early dial_pause_s is too short for your handset A flash does nothing the handset's flash is shorter than flash_min_ms or longer than flash_max_ms; the Tools tab reads the chip's hook state Nothing on the handset display cid, then cid_when, then the transmit test The LED will not follow the line led names a lamp that exists on this board; '' means leave it alone A restriction you set is not honoured health reports the network's provisioning word. That is the operator, not the router

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
Can I use any phone on the AW1000's RJ11 socket?

An ordinary analogue phone with a tone dial and an RJ11 plug. A handset with a display shows the caller id, if the signalling mode matches what the phone expects. Pulse-dialling phones are not supported.

How do I get a three-way call on the AW1000?

Switch on 3-way calling in Phone settings → Features — it is off as installed — then take the second call and press the handset's flash key followed by 3. Both calls must be up.

Why does my phone not ring back a held call?

Recall works when the call was put on hold by the handset. A call the browser page put on hold stays the page's — lifting the handset gives you the recall dial tone for the handset's own held call, not the page's.

Does the caller id work with the number in international form?

The message on the line carries digits. The numbering plan decides how they are displayed, and region set to auto follows the network the line registered on.

docs.title: Health, tests and the log
docs.text: The Health tab reports facts, not an opinion. Where two things could disagree — the rate you asked for and the rate the modem actually puts on the bus — both are shown separately, so a mismatch is visible instead of inferred.

docs.title: Modem AT port
docs.text: field what it answers Port the tty the daemon found for the modem's USB interface USB interface at_interface, as configured Responding did the last question get an answer Last reply seconds since one did Port owner free, or the guard's word for what is holding it

docs.title: Line
docs.text:
field what it answers Line chip Answering or Not answering — is the chip replying on the register bus Hook the hook state the chip reports, per channel State the line's state as the daemon sees it Quiet hours whether the line is quiet now, and what decided it: window, all-day or manual Numbering the numbering plan in force, and whether it came from the network or from your setting Calibration whether the chip calibrated at start Battery the DC voltage on the pair, in volts Loop current what flows through a connected handset, in milliamps

Battery and Loop current are the two that tell you whether an unresponsive phone is the phone's fault or the line's.

docs.title: Modem, SIM and VoLTE
docs.text:
field what it answers SIM is the card ready Network registration is the modem registered for service VoLTE registration is it registered in the IMS — the one that makes voice possible Signal (RSRP) the serving cell's RSRP in dBm Network / Operator the RAT and the operator name the network reported Audio mode three separate facts: hdVoice as on, set or off (the wish, and whether it was honoured), audioRate (8000 or 16000), voiceLayout Call waiting what the network itself says is provisioned, read back rather than assumed CLIR the setting, and the network's provisioning word: not_provisioned, provisioned, unknown, restricted or allowed

Why the rate is three fields

Asking for HD voice is a wish. The modem is asked which rate it actually puts on the bus, the line comes up at that rate only if the answers agree, and only while nobody is using the line. Seeing the wish, the answer and the layout together is how you tell a refused wish from a broken line.

docs.title: System
docs.text:
field what it answers Kernel module is awvoice-fxs loaded Audio bridge is it running Frames carried how many 20 ms frames have crossed it Resyncs how often the two sides lost step and were realigned Frames skipped playback frames the ring was empty for — counted silence, never a stale frame from an earlier call Longest gap the biggest hole seen between slots, in microseconds

These four counters are the difference between "the audio is odd" and "the bridge is resyncing every few seconds". They read as empty when the statistics cannot be read at all, which is itself the answer.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Two rows, one for the recordings folder and one for the messages folder: the path, whether it is ready, how many megabytes are free, and the error if it is not. A drive that is not mounted says so in words; anything else reports the operating system's reason.

The folders are made and checked when the service starts or reloads, and again before a call writes a file.

docs.title: Service
docs.text:
Start, Stop, Restart — each with a confirmation, and each gated:

button disabled when Start the service is already up Stop, Restart a call is in progress, or the line is ringing

Stop and restart are refused while a call is active, from the same check the page uses to grey the buttons out.

docs.title: Counters
docs.text: field what it counts Modem timeouts AT questions that went unanswered Hook gaps over 20 ms how often the 5 ms clock missed a hook sample — the number that explains a choppy hook flash Longest hook gap (ms) the worst one seen Faults the daemon's own fault count

docs.title: SIP and the guards
docs.text: field what it answers Who holds the name (qmodem_voip) awvoice, voipd or none. This decides whether a network phone can be offered Who holds the voice port whether another process has the modem's voice AT port Last refusal the fixed word from the last denied action Browser audio the mode, whether a session is live, the port and the address

docs.title: The log
docs.text:
The tab's folded Recent log shows the last 40 lines of the service's own log, with every run of digits masked to [number] — so a log can be pasted into a report without carrying a phone number.

Over SSH the same thing, wider:

logread -e awvoice-phoned | tail -50     # the daemon
logread -e cw-led                        # the LED daemon, if the panel looks wrong

docs.title: The tests
docs.text:
On Test tools, and all three need the line idle.

test what it proves Ring test the chip can drive the ringer for 5 seconds. Keep the handset on the hook: a phone's ringer can draw more than the chip's AC ring detector tolerates, and when that happens the burst is cut and the log says the chip's ring trip fired before any lift. That sentence is a fact about the phone, not a dead line Line test the electrical state: hook, battery voltage, loop current, whether it matches what the board file expects, and whether a leak is suspected Test call loopback, so you hear your own voice after a short delay. This build does not offer it — the card is disabled and tagged Not available yet

docs.title: What has been measured on a router
docs.text:
These are the checks that were actually run on a real AW1000, and they are the reason the pages say what they say:

check result a call made and taken with the RJ11 socket empty, from the browser page and from a soft phone both directions worked the handset taking over a call the browser page held the call continued at the phone, the page's microphone and speaker stopped, and the log named the handset as the one that answered hold, resume, taking a waiting call, swapping two, and the three-way join from the page worked, with 3-way calling switched on a wideband call brought up at 16 kHz and recorded the recording carried both voices at the rate the modem answered a soft phone registering with the vendor VoIP engine on the boot path registered, no audio — which is what the first-boot script that takes it off the boot path fixes the SIP switch moved while a call was in progress the switch reported waiting and the service moved when the call ended the answering machine answering, and a lift in the middle of a message the message ended at the lift and the rest of the conversation was not recorded quiet hours in all three modes silent held the line quiet and the page offered Answer; machine mode handed the call to the machine; reject released the caller

What has not been measured

The handset's transmit band above 4 kHz has not been confirmed with an instrument, and the loopback test call has never been run because the build does not offer it. Where a page claims a number, it is one that was read from a device or from the shipped source.

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
How do I check the AW1000's phone port without a handset?

Health tells you the chip is answering, the hook state, the battery voltage and the loop current without anything on the line. The Ring test and Line test are on the Test tools tab.

Why does the Health tab show two different audio rates?

Because they are two different facts: what you asked for and what the modem answered with. The line runs at the modem's answer, and a wish that was not honoured is shown as one.

Is it safe to send you the log?

The page's own log view masks every run of digits. logread on the router does not, so read it before you paste it, and never include a password or a full IMEI.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The call is carried by the router's 5G modem over VoLTE, which the phone daemon controls through the modem's AT port. The router drives the line-interface chip of the RJ11 socket and bridges the two in the kernel, so an ordinary phone behaves like an ordinary phone. There is no Asterisk and no PBX: the cellular network is the exchange, and the SIM's own number is the line's number.

docs.title: The three packages
docs.text:
package licence what it owns kmod-awvoice-fxs GPL-2.0-only the line chip's register bus, the PCM block, the audio bridge between modem and chip, the capture tap that feeds the recordings and messages, the playback ring that carries a greeting and the page's voice to the caller, and the hardware ring watchdog awvoice-phoned see licence the hook, the tones, dialling, ringing, caller id, the call log, the recordings, the answering machine, quiet hours, the browser audio stream, the front end a network phone speaks through, and the ubus service awvoice luci-app-awvoice as above the LuCI page

The module is built for one exact kernel build, which is why apk refuses it on any other kernel rather than installing something that cannot load.

docs.title: A watchdog, not a promise
docs.text:
A thin kernel module owns the register bus, the PCM block and a hardware ring watchdog: if the phone service ever stops, the chip is back in reset within milliseconds. A line cannot be left ringing, and a line cannot be left live with nothing behind it.

That is the whole safety argument for running the daemon as an ordinary service: the failure mode is a silent line, not a screaming one.

docs.title: The 20 ms frame is the unit everywhere
docs.text:
The kernel bridge hands out one frame per 125 µs slot: 160 samples at 8 kHz, two time samples per slot at 16 kHz. The capture side and the playback side are the only two places that convert it, and nothing else counts slots.

path what it carries the caller's voice inward a lock-free capture ring to the daemon, which is also where the recording's channels come from a greeting or the page's voice outward a matching playback ring into the bridge an empty ring silence, with a counted underrun — never a stale frame from an earlier call. Both rings are reset when the bridges stop and start

This is why the browser stream, the recording file and the kernel all speak in the same 20 ms unit: there is one number to get right, and one place that converts it.

docs.title: The front end's socket
docs.text:
Between the daemon and the front end that carries a network phone: one message per 20 ms frame over a unix seqpacket socket — a stream at the same path would be refused by the kernel. It is non-blocking throughout, with no threads and no clock of its own.

header twelve little-endian bytes: magic 0x514d534b, version, type, payload length payload 160 samples of 16-bit linear audio. The interface carries 8 kHz only, so any other count is refused with an error frame and the peer closed heartbeat carries nothing, answers nothing, and refreshes the binding it belongs to bindings eight live at once

The two programs meet here and over ubus. The phone port contains none of the SIP service's code, and the SIP service contains none of the phone port's.

docs.title: One gate for every action
docs.text:
Answer, dial, hang up, DTMF and route each carry the call revision the asker saw, and a refusal never changes the call.

case the rule a hang-up for a call that has already ended accepted. The intent is satisfied, and two people ending a call at the same moment is not an error answering a call that is not ringing refused, rather than answered early a front end asking for more than the call carries refused. It may take less, never more a revision that is absent refused. A revision is never 0

docs.title: HD voice is a wish, and the modem decides
docs.text:
The chip's band, the PCM slots and the audio bridge are one layout, and the slots can only change while the bus is down.

  1. The service asks the modem, read-only, which rate it actually puts on the bus.
  2. The line is brought up at that rate only if the modem answered with the rate that was asked for, and only while nobody is using the line.
  3. A change that comes while the handset is up waits for the line to clear.
  4. Changing the rate does restart the modem, so mobile data drops for about half a minute.
  5. A modem that keeps answering with the other rate is asked a bounded number of times, and the line then keeps working at the rate it has, with the reason in the log.

The health reply carries the setting, the modem's answer and the layout the path came up at as three separate facts, which is what makes a refused wish visible instead of mysterious.

docs.title: The board file, and the chip's firmware
docs.text:
The line chip needs this board's own values — line voltages, ringing, tones, impedances, the init sequence — in a board file.

where it comes from a ready board file ships with awvoice-phoned, and the first service start installs it at /etc/awvoice/board.bin. A file already there is never overwritten why it is in this repository its contents are operating parameters — functional values the hardware requires — not the chip maker's executable code. The values were read from the board's own stock firmware deriving your own tools/provision/awvoice-board-extract.py with the section map tools/provision/aw1000.map produce the same format from your router's original firmware the chip's firmware it runs on the firmware built into the chip. This port uses no DSP patch file: none is needed and none ships if a chip does not come ready the service stops with that cause in the log, instead of leaving a silent dead line

docs.title: The 5 ms clock
docs.text:
All the line logic sits in one daemon on a single 5 ms clock. The hook is sampled on it, the tones are stepped on it, and the counters on the Health tab are about it: a hook gap over 20 ms is the number that explains a choppy flash, and the longest gap is its worst case.

The same core that runs on that clock builds and runs on an ordinary computer with no hardware attached, which is how the call logic is tested at all: the state machine is handed a synthetic hook and a synthetic modem, and the assertions are about what it tells the line to do.

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
Does the phone port need a PBX or an Asterisk?

No. The cellular network is the exchange and the SIM's number is the line's number. The router drives the line chip and bridges the audio in the kernel, and the daemon holds the call logic.

Why is the audio path in the kernel rather than in the daemon?

Because 20 ms frames have to land in the right slot, and the same frames have to reach the recording mirror and the playback ring without a copy through user space. The daemon gets the frames; the kernel counts the slots.

What happens if the phone daemon crashes during a call?

The watchdog resets the line chip within milliseconds, so the phone stops ringing and the line goes quiet. The service is restarted by the init system, and the call is gone with the modem session that carried it.

docs.title: Network phones
docs.text:
The line has one number and any number of phones on it. This page is about the third of them: a soft phone on your own network — a laptop or a phone running a SIP app — ringing and dialing through the same SIM line as the handset and the browser page.

Nothing speaks SIP until you say so

A router as installed has no SIP port open and no SIP process running. awvoice.sip.mode ships as web, which means the page and the handset only. Everything on this page happens after you move that switch.

docs.title: What the switch actually does
docs.text:
The SIP tab's first card asks one question — who may use the phone line — and has two answers:

the card says the option writes what happens next SIP off — the page and the handset awvoice.sip.mode = web the service is stopped, and the front-end name this port publishes is withdrawn SIP on — a network phone joins them interop, or baresip if that is the word already stored the service is started

Saving is one action with a fixed order, and the card tells you where it got to:

  1. the side is written to /etc/config/awvoice;
  2. the page waits for the daemon to publish or withdraw the front-end object qmodem_voip — eight tries, 250 ms apart;
  3. the service's own init script, /etc/init.d/qmodem_voip_sipd, is started or stopped.

While step 3 is pending the card re-checks every two seconds for up to a minute, and after a move it re-reads every 1.5 seconds up to six times. The outcome word is always shown:

the card says what it means started / stopped the service moved as asked waiting a call is in progress. The service moves when the call ends rather than being cut in half absent there is no SIP service installed on this router denied this account may not start or stop it — the permission is a separate grant failed the service did not answer. The move is yours to make

A word the build does not know is refused, not ignored

awvoice.sip.mode accepts web, interop and baresip. Anything else is refused, said so in the log, and the line stays on the side it was on.

docs.title: What the service is
docs.text:
The network phone is carried by a separate program on the router — the SIP service that comes with the QModem feed. This page's software does not contain any of it, does not reconfigure it, and does not store its secrets. The relationship is exactly two things:

who may use the line decided here, in awvoice.sip.mode how a network phone signs in decided there, in /etc/config/qmodem_sip

The AWvoice page reads that file's settings back and shows them, and it is the only place you can change them without a shell. The values this image ships are in UCI options.

docs.title: Calls coming in
docs.text: setting default Allow the calls coming in on the inbound direction Network lan which interface it listens on SIP port 5060 UDP and TCP together, shown as fixed text Account name awvoice the name a soft phone signs in with. It is named for this router's phone service Password CleanWRT#40 the same secret as the default Wi-Fi key, so a router has one pair to remember

docs.title: Calls going out through a provider
docs.text: setting default Allow the calls going out off the outbound direction Network wan SIP port 5061 Provider address unset server and port Encryption TLS fixed Account name, Realm, Password unset the image ships no outbound secret at all — the direction that reaches a server outside the house starts empty Re-register every 300 s

docs.title: Passwords, and what is never shown
docs.text:
The password field shows stored — type to replace, or not set. A stored password is never displayed, because it cannot be read back: it is stored in a form that cannot be reversed. Type it once if you need to see it, or press Create a new password to get a fresh one.

The credential the service actually uses lives at /var/run/qmodem_voip/sip.conf — a derived file in memory-backed storage, regenerated from /etc/config/qmodem_sip when the service starts and when its configuration is reloaded. The page reports whether that file is in place. It never reads it.

docs.title: The two guards
docs.text:
A second front end on one line can fight the first, so two checks decide whether the network side may run at all. They are checks, not negotiation: this port never opens, closes, stops or reconfigures another program's things.

guard the question what a bad answer means the voice AT port is another process holding the modem's voice AT port? the phone daemon cannot run the modem, so the network side is not started the front-end name is the object name qmodem_voip already registered by something else? the network side may not offer it. The page and the handset still work — the name decides only the network half

Both are asked again at service start, on a settings reload, on a modem hotplug, and on the daemon's slow re-check. The Health and Diagnostics panes report the current answers, so a refusal is a fact you can read rather than a thing you infer.

The vendor VoIP engine is off the boot path in this image

A qmodem_voip engine that starts before the phone daemon takes the name, and a soft phone then registers but never gets audio. This image stops that engine and removes it from the boot path on first boot, precisely so the phone daemon can answer the name itself. See first-boot defaults.

docs.title: What a soft phone needs to be set to
docs.text:
field value SIP server / domain the router's LAN address Port 5060 UDP (or TCP) User / auth id the Account name on the page (awvoice as shipped) Password the Password on the page Display name anything you like

A call placed from the soft phone goes out over the SIM; a call to the SIM's number rings the soft phone as well as the handset. Whoever answers first has the call, and the handset-wins-a-lift rule is what keeps that from becoming a contest.

docs.title: The code a phone scans
docs.text:
Typing the five fields above into a phone is the last part of the job nobody enjoys. The SIP tab's Show a Linphone QR code button removes it.

what the code holds one URL and nothing else, because a provisioning URL is what that app expects to read from a code what the phone does with it fetches the file at that address and builds the account itself. Nothing is typed where the file is written /www/awvoice-provision/awvoice-<32 hex>.xml, by /usr/libexec/awvoice-provision, under a random name how it is served a plain HTTP listener on port 8080, with directory listings off and the private-network filter on, whose document root is that one directory how long it lives ten minutes. The card names the minute it stops being served, and the daemon's own round runs every 60 seconds and retires the files this feature wrote. Nothing else in that folder is touched what the file contains the account name, its realm and its password in clear

Show a code while the phone is beside you

The provisioning file carries the account password in clear text and is readable by anything on the LAN for those ten minutes. It is never reachable from outside your network, but it is not a secret once it is on the wire. Show it when you are holding both devices.

If the app already holds an account

That app offers its scanner only while it holds no account at all. Remove the existing account in the app first, then scan.

When no code can be made, the card says why in words instead of showing a broken picture:

the card says what to do the network phones are switched off move the switch on first there is no account name yet set one on the page the stored password cannot be read back type it once, or press Create a new password the network has no address right now the interface the page reads has no IPv4 yet this router serves no plain address a phone can fetch the port-8080 listener is not in /etc/config/uhttpd. That listener belongs to the web server's own configuration

An older configuration is migrated on upgrade The phone registers and cannot place a call something else holds the front-end name qmodem_voip — usually the vendor engine, started by hand. The Diagnostics pane names the holder The switch says denied the account you are logged in as may not start or stop that service. See the API and who may call it The switch says waiting forever a call is in progress and will not be cut. End it, or leave it and the service moves when the call ends Inbound calls do not reach the phone the inbound direction is off, or the account name and password in the app do not match what the page shows Outbound through a provider fails the outbound direction ships with no server, no realm and no password. It is configured, not enabled The QR card refuses to make a code it said why, in words. See the table above

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
Can I use a soft phone with the AW1000's RJ11 port?

Yes, once the AWvoice page's SIP switch is on. The soft phone registers to the router over your own LAN and rings and dials through the SIM's line, beside the handset and the browser page. No provider account and no second number are involved.

Does the AW1000 expose a SIP port to the internet?

No. The listener is on the LAN interface, and the switch that opens it is off as installed. The outbound direction, which is the one that reaches outside your house, ships with no server and no secret at all.

Why does my soft phone register but I hear nothing?

Almost always the audio path: the SIP service must hand media to the phone daemon's socket, and that is one setting in /etc/config/qmodem_sip. This image ships it correctly; a configuration carried over from an older release is migrated at first boot.

How do I set up a Linphone account without typing a password?

SIP → Show a Linphone QR code. The phone reads one URL, fetches its own account file, and builds the account. The address stops being served ten minutes later, and the card names the minute it stops.

docs.title: Quiet hours
docs.text:
Quiet hours hold the handset, the answering machine and the network phones off a ringing call for windows of the day you write. It is not a do-not-disturb flag on one device: it is the line itself deciding not to make noise.

The controls are on Rules → Quiet hours. Nothing is honoured out of the box: with no window written, the phone rings at every hour.

docs.title: A window
docs.text:
field what it means Enabled a per-window switch, so you can keep a window written without it acting All day the whole 24 hours. The two time fields disappear when you tick it From / To HH:MM to HH:MM. A from later than its to runs through midnight — 22:00 to 07:00 is tonight into tomorrow morning, not nothing Days which weekdays count. Three-letter names only: sun mon tue wed thu fri sat Mode what happens to a call that arrives inside the window. See below Again in minutes before the same caller is let through again. New windows start at 15; 0 turns that answer off

Up to eight windows. The first window that covers the moment decides, in the order they are written, so a narrow window has to sit above the broad one that would also match.

docs.title: The three modes
docs.text:
mode what happens to a call that arrives inside the window Silent the line stays silent. The page says Call held quiet, its Answer button takes the call, and lifting the handset answers it too Answering machine the call goes to the machine. This needs the machine switched on; with it off the caller hears nothing from this side until the network ends the call Reject the caller is released

The machine mode is a promise you have to keep elsewhere

A window set to Answering machine on a router whose machine is off leaves the caller listening to nothing. If you want the machine to take night calls, switch it on in Phone settings → Answering machine as well.

docs.title: Who reaches you anyway
docs.text:
an emergency number always. Nothing on this router blocks one, whatever a window says a number on the ring through list the window's own list, and the page's Always ring through list, joined into one list of at most twenty numbers a number of a contact marked Ring through quiet hours recognised however the network happened to write the number, because the match is made in international form the same caller, again a caller who tries a second time inside the window's Again in minutes gets through. This is what makes a genuine emergency from a fixed line survive a silent window

The Always ring through button is disabled while no window exists — there is nothing to ring through to.

docs.title: Doing it by hand: *78, *79 and #
docs.text:
you dial what happens *78 ask for quiet now, whatever the windows say *79 give that up either, followed by # the same, with the send key. Both forms are accepted

They work on the handset and in the page's dialler. A hand-asked quiet is remembered across a save of anything else, and falls back to the written windows when the service restarts — the ask is not stored as a window.

docs.title: The clock rule
docs.text:
Nothing is honoured from a schedule before the router knows what time it is.

An unknown clock never quiets the line

A router whose clock still reads 1970 would match every window or none, so with an untrusted clock the line rings normally. A quiet you asked for by hand needs no clock at all, because it is not a schedule.

The Health tab reports what the line answered a moment ago and what decided it: whether quiet is on, the cause — window, all-day or manual — and what was asked for.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Quiet hours are one dnd section per window in /etc/config/awvoice:

# one window: weekdays, 22:00 to 07:00, the machine answers, the same caller may try again in 15 minutes
config dnd 'night'
        option enabled '1'
        option from '22:00'
        option to '07:00'
        option days 'mon tue wed thu fri'
        option mode 'machine'
        option repeat_min '15'
        list allow '+94771234567'

config contact 'family'
        option name 'Family'
        option ring_through '1'
option values default meaning enabled 0|1 1 on the page does this window act from, to HH:MM 22:00, 07:00 on the page the window. Past midnight is normal all_day 0|1 0 the whole day days three-letter weekday names all seven on the page which days mode silent, machine, reject silent when unset what happens inside repeat_min 0–1440 15 on the page minutes before the same caller is let through; 0 is off allow a list of numbers empty ring through. Twenty across all windows

A contact section with ring_through '1' needs nothing written in any window.

docs.title: When it does not do what you expect
docs.text: symptom what it means The phone rings during a window you wrote the window's enabled, or its days, or an earlier window that also covers the moment and says something else Nothing rings, ever a window with all_day, or a window whose times cover 24 hours. Check the order The caller hears nothing at all mode is Answering machine and the machine is off, or mode is Silent and nobody takes it A number on the ring-through list still gets held the stored form does not match. Matching is done in international form, so 0771234567 and +94771234567 are the same caller only when the numbering plan says so Quiet came on at the wrong hour the router's clock. Set your time zone *78 did nothing the digits were collected as a dialled number. A service code needs to be dialled as a code, and the send key does not act inside it

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
Can I stop the AW1000's phone from ringing at night?

Yes. Rules → Quiet hours takes up to eight windows with times, weekdays or all day, and three answers for a call that arrives inside one: stay silent, send it to the answering machine, or release the caller.

Can some numbers still get through quiet hours?

Yes: a per-window ring through list, a page-wide Always ring through list — twenty numbers across them — any contact marked Ring through quiet hours, and the same caller trying a second time within the window's repeat minutes.

Does quiet hours stop the answering machine too?

It depends on the window's mode. Silent holds everything quiet, Answering machine sends the call to the machine, and Reject releases the caller. The handset, the browser page and the network phones all follow the same decision.

What is *78 on a phone?

The code that asks for quiet now, without writing a window. *79 gives it up. Both work on the handset and in the page's dialler, with or without the send key.

docs.title: Recordings and the answering machine
docs.text:
Both of these listen to a call the router already carries, and both are off until you switch them on. They live on the Settings tab, and everything they produce is reachable from the call's own card rather than from a folder you have to remember.

Know the rules where you connect this

Recording a conversation is regulated almost everywhere, and often requires telling the other side. Nothing on this router announces that a call is being recorded — an announcement is a greeting you record and play yourself. Check what applies to you before you switch either feature on.

docs.title: Call recordings
docs.text:
option default what it does record_enabled 0 record the calls this line answers record_path /etc/awvoice/recordings where the files go record_max_mb 50 the folder's budget. Passing it removes the oldest files until the folder fits

What a recording is:

container a WAV file, playable anywhere channels stereo — the caller on one channel, this side on the other, so the two are separable in any editor rate 16 kHz when HD voice is in use, 8 kHz otherwise. The file carries the rate the call actually came up at, not the wish naming <epoch>-<call id>.wav. No file name ever carries a phone number what is captured the call from the moment it is answered. A call that is never answered is not recorded; a call the machine answers becomes a message instead where it is attached the call's own card in the log, with play, save and delete

This side means the line, not the handset

The second channel is taken from the audio the router puts on the line, so a call answered from the browser page or a soft phone is recorded with that side's voice too. A handset that is on the table while a network phone talks records the network phone.

Recordings are kept on flash under /etc/awvoice/, which a keep-settings upgrade carries across. The 50 MB budget is per folder and is deliberately small: this is a router with a fixed amount of flash, and a recording folder that grows silently is the fastest way to fill it.

docs.title: The answering machine
docs.text:
option default what it does machine_enabled 0 let the line answer for you machine_delay 10 seconds of ringing before the machine takes the call. 0 answers at once machine_max_s 120 the longest single message machine_max_mb 50 the folder's budget, oldest message removed past it machine_path /etc/awvoice/messages where the messages go

The machine answers, plays the greeting, and records what the caller says after the tone. Each message is attached to the call it came from, so the log row tells you who rang, when, and that a message is waiting.

docs.title: The greeting
docs.text:
There is exactly one greeting file, at a fixed place: /etc/awvoice/greeting.wav. It is not an option, and there is no list of greetings.

a new router the package carries a short default greeting, and the first service start that finds nothing at that path copies it in. So the machine works the moment you switch it on after that the file is yours. An upgrade never writes over it no greeting at all the machine does not answer. Silence is the safe answer, not a beep into an empty line

Three controls sit on the card, and each one has a rule the daemon enforces:

control what it does Play hears the file exactly as it stands on the router — including a file the machine cannot use, which is how you recognise one. Disabled when there is nothing there to read Upload WAV… the browser decodes and resamples to 8 kHz mono, so a recording from a phone or a computer in any usual rate works. The daemon checks the result again, writes a temporary file and moves it into place, so an interrupted upload cannot leave a half greeting Record takes your voice from the computer's microphone. The service trims the silence off both ends, adds a short gap, and adds the tone that tells the caller to start talking

What the machine will accept:

format 16-bit PCM WAV rate 8 kHz or 16 kHz size at most 2 MB if it cannot read it the machine switches itself off rather than answer with noise, and the card says which file it found and what was wrong

An uploaded file is kept as its author made it

The trim-and-tone treatment belongs to the Record path, because that one captures silence at both ends by accident. A file you upload or copy onto the router yourself is played as it is: whatever tone and pause you put in is what the caller hears.

The shell route, if you would rather keep your own recording out of the browser:

scp greeting.wav root@192.168.1.1:/etc/awvoice/greeting.wav
/etc/init.d/awvoice restart

docs.title: Taking a call over from the machine
docs.text:
Lift the handset while the machine is talking to a caller and the call becomes yours. The message ends at the lift, and the rest of the conversation is not recorded — the same behaviour as a standard voicemail system, kept deliberately: a call you are standing in the middle of is a call, not a message.

The page's Answer button does the same thing from the browser, and the handset-wins-a-lift rule decides what happens when both are reaching for the same call.

docs.title: Hearing a message
docs.text: A message is played from the call's card in the log, next to the caller's number and the time it arrived: play in the browser, save the file, or delete it. There is no separate voicemail page and no mailbox to log into.

docs.title: When it misbehaves

The card says which The card says the greeting cannot be used the file is not 16-bit PCM, or its rate is not 8 or 16 kHz, or it is over 2 MB. Play still works, which is how you hear what is wrong Callers hear nothing after the greeting they are not talking yet, or the message cap was reached and the recording stopped. Check machine_max_s Recording is on but no file appears the call was not answered from this side. A missed call is never recorded Old recordings disappeared the size budget removed them. Raise record_max_mb if the folder is too small for how you work The router's flash is filling look at /etc/awvoice/recordings and /etc/awvoice/messages first: both are on flash, and both are the only large things this feature writes

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
Does the AW1000 record phone calls?

It can, once you switch recording on. Each answered call is kept on the router as a stereo WAV — the caller and this side on separate channels — with a folder budget that removes the oldest. Nothing leaves the router, and no file name carries a number.

Can the AW1000 act as an answering machine?

Yes. After a delay you set, an unanswered call hears your greeting and leaves a message, which is played, saved or deleted from that call's card in the log. A greeting ships with the package, so it works the moment you switch it on.

What happens if I pick up while the machine is recording?

The call transfers to you and the message ends at the lift. The rest of the conversation is not recorded.

What audio format does the greeting need?

16-bit PCM WAV at 8 or 16 kHz, at most 2 MB. The page's upload path resamples for you; a file the machine cannot read switches the machine off instead of playing noise.

docs.title: Rules and the phone book
docs.text: Rules is four panes behind one row of chips: Phone book, Call blocking, Alarm call and Quiet hours. The last has its own page; this page is the other three.

docs.title: The phone book
docs.text:
limit value contacts 100 numbers per contact 3 name length 32 characters a speed-dial code exactly 2 digits, and unique across the book control what it does Add contact opens the editor: Name, Numbers (up to 3), Add number — which disappears at three — Speed dial code, and Ring through quiet hours a row's tags Speed 27 when the contact has a code, Rings through quiet hours when it carries the flag Edit / Delete per contact

A number may be stored with a label — +94771234567:mobile, :home, :work — and the label is what the display shows beside the number.

docs.title: Speed dial
docs.text:
Two digits, then the send key. 27# dials the contact whose code is 27, and the same two digits dialled alone are an ordinary number after the pause ends it. The page's dialler and the handset's keypad behave the same way.

An emergency number is never replaced

A speed-dial entry cannot stand in for an emergency number, and a dialled emergency number is never rewritten by anything in the phone book. That is a property of the design, not a guarantee of service.

A stored number longer than the dial buffer (20 digits) is refused with a line in the log rather than silently truncated.

docs.title: Matching a caller
docs.text: The name shown in the call log and on the handset's display comes from matching the digits the network sent, in international form, against the book. That is why a contact can be recognised however the network happened to write the number — local or with the country code — and why the same match drives the ring-through flag in quiet hours.

docs.title: Call blocking
docs.text:
control what it does Anonymous calls — Block calls without caller ID releases a call that arrives with no number Incoming numbers a list of 50 numbers that never ring this line Incoming prefixes a list of 50 prefixes — the usual way to silence a whole range Outgoing numbers numbers this line will not dial Outgoing prefixes prefixes it will not dial

Each list has its own Edit button and each save is applied immediately, without a page-wide save.

What the rules do, exactly:

when they are applied incoming rules before the line rings at all; outgoing rules at the moment the digits are about to go out what a blocked outgoing dial looks like nothing is sent to the network. You hear the congestion tone, and the call is logged with outcome blocked and cause 34 how numbers are compared in international form, so a prefix written one way matches a call written another per-call restriction prefixes a dialled #31# or *31# is understood as a CLIR request and stripped before any rule looks at the number emergency numbers never blocked. A rule that would match one does not

Blocking is not screening

A blocked call is released quietly. The caller is not told they were blocked, and nothing about the rule is visible to them. There is no announcement, no record on their side, and no way to recover a call a rule released — which is why the lists are limited to 50 entries each and the page shows them plainly.

docs.title: Alarm calls
docs.text:
A wake-up call rings the line at a time you set. Up to 20 alarms, each with a label of up to 32 characters, a time in 24-hour form, a set of weekdays, and its own enable switch.

how it is checked every 30 seconds what happens the line rings, for up to 60 seconds. There is no caller id on it how often one ring per minute, whatever the number of alarms that came due when it is skipped the line is busy, or the handset is off hook, or the clock is not trusted the clock trusted when the router's own year has reached 2026. An untrusted clock skips the alarm once and says so

The editor shows the router's clock beside your browser's and warns when they differ by more than five minutes, because an alarm is a promise about time.

docs.title: Forwarding, and why there is no pane for it
docs.text:
Call forwarding is a network service: the router asks the operator to divert your calls, and the operator's answer is what decides whether anything happens. This build reads it — the forwarding_get reply carries whether the network has it on, to what number, with what delay, and what error came back — but the Rules tab does not offer a forwarding editor. A forwarding rule stored in /etc/config/awvoice is still read by the daemon.

If you need forwarding, set it on the network with the service code your operator publishes; the handset page explains how codes are dialled.

docs.title: When a rule does not act
docs.text: symptom what it means A number you blocked still rings the stored form does not match what the network sent. Compare in international form, or use a prefix An outgoing call you expected to be blocked went through the rule list is on the outgoing side and the number matched an incoming list, or a #31# prefix changed the digits before matching A speed dial does nothing the two digits need the send key, and the code must be unique The alarm did not fire the line was busy, the handset was off hook, or the clock was not trusted. All three are logged The alarm fired at the wrong time the router's clock or the time zone. The editor's warning compares it with your browser Block calls without caller ID does nothing the network delivered a number after all. Check the log row: a withheld caller is shown as Withheld

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
Can I stop certain numbers from ringing my AW1000?

Yes. Rules → Call blocking takes 50 incoming numbers and 50 incoming prefixes, the same for outgoing, and a switch for anonymous callers. Incoming rules act before the line ever rings, and the call is logged as blocked.

Can the AW1000 wake me up with a phone call?

Yes, with alarm calls: up to 20, each with a time and the days it should fire. The line rings for up to a minute. It trusts the router's clock, so set your time zone first.

How does speed dial work on this phone?

Two digits per contact, unique across the book, dialled followed by the send key — on the handset and in the page's dialler. The same two digits alone are an ordinary number.

Can I block an emergency number by mistake?

No. Nothing on this router blocks an emergency number, and a dialled emergency number is never replaced by a speed-dial entry.

docs.title: Settings reference
docs.text:
Everything is in one file, /etc/config/awvoice. The page writes the same file, so uci and LuCI never disagree. An option with an invalid value is reported in the log and its default is used instead:

logread -e awvoice | tail -20

The shipped file carries only four settings — flash_min_ms 80, flash_max_ms 300, led green:phone and sip.mode web. Every other value below is a compiled default, which is why an option that is absent from your file is not a bug.

docs.title: Settings the page does not show
docs.text:
at_interface and led are the two that usually matter, and both ship with working values for the AW1000. Also clir, level_trace, the four web_* values beyond the port, mic_gain_db and earpiece_gain_db, page_refresh_s (which is in Phone settings → Advanced), and the whole forwarding section.

uci show awvoice                          # everything as stored
uci set awvoice.main.conference=1         # turn the three-way join on
uci commit awvoice
/etc/init.d/awvoice restart

A shell commit does not reload the page

uci commit writes the file. Only the page's own save applies and reloads, and a hand edit needs the service restart above. See first-boot defaults for the same trap in the other direction.
