docs.title: Still stuck
docs.text:
1. Take the Health tab's screenshot or ubus call awvoice health output.
  2. Grab the log: logread -e awvoice-phoned, and read it before you paste it — the shell version is not masked.
  3. Say which release you are on (cat /etc/openwrt_release) and which of the three front ends you were using: handset, browser page, or network phone.
  4. Open an issue on GitHub. Never paste a password, a key or a full IMEI.

docs.title: The web phone
docs.text:
The Overview tab is not a status page that happens to mention calls. It is a handset: a keypad, a three-button call rail, a flash key, a microphone mute and two level meters, carrying the same line the RJ11 socket does.

With nothing plugged into the RJ11 socket, this is a complete telephone. That is not a fallback: the line is carried by the modem, and the page is one of the three things that can hold it.

The page must be open over HTTPS

A browser takes no microphone from a page it does not trust, and it sends audio to an encrypted socket only from an encrypted page. Open LuCI over https://.

docs.title: The controls
docs.text:
control what it does the number field what you are dialing. Up to 32 digits, with a backspace that deletes the last one the keypad 1–9, *, 0, # with their letter groups, and 0 giving + for an international prefix Call / Answer one button, in one slot. It is Call on an idle line and Answer while a call rings Flash the handset's flash key. Hold, swap, take the waiting call, take a held call back — and a digit typed after it is a code Hang up / Reject / Cancel the same slot again: Hang up in a call, Reject while a call rings, Cancel while your own attempt is still setting up Use this computer's microphone and speaker opens the audio session. Without it the call exists but you cannot hear it Mute / Unmute suspends the microphone alone. You still hear the caller Stop audio closes the session. The call goes on; the page just stops carrying it the level meters two live bars, so you can see both directions of audio while the call is up Technical details a folded row of counters: who owns the answer, the call revision, frames to the audio side, frames from it, frames dropped

A control that cannot act right now keeps its place and is disabled rather than hidden, so the layout never jumps under your cursor:

when what is disabled a call is ringing in, or your own attempt is setting up, or the call is being torn down the keypad nothing is active, held or waiting Flash the handset, the answering machine or another front end already holds the answer Answer no audio session exists yet Mute and Stop audio are not shown at all

docs.title: Flash, and the codes that follow it
docs.text:
The page's Flash button stands in for a physical hook break, and the codes are the handset's:

after the flash what happens 1 end the current call and take the other one 2 hold this call and take the other; with two live calls it swaps them, with one held call it takes it back 3 join the two calls into a three-way conversation. Needs 3-way calling switched on, which it is not as installed 0 refuse the waiting call, or release the held one

The window for the digit is three seconds, and the page says so under the keypad while it is open. This is the same window the handset's flash key uses, described on the handset page.

docs.title: Who owns the line
docs.text:
Two rules hold the whole thing together, and both are visible in the log.

The handset wins a lift. Lifting the handset during a page call carries the call on at the phone. The log records the handset as the one that answered it, that call's card says so, and the page's microphone and speaker stop with it. A call the page put on hold is not taken by a lift: the lift gets the recall dial tone and the held call stays the page's.

One owner of the playback ring. Exactly one thing may send audio toward the caller at a time: nothing, the greeting, a network phone, or this page. The handset sits on the same ladder, which is why a lift ends a browser session cleanly instead of fighting it.

The page cannot take a call the handset already holds, and it never interrupts a call in progress. What its Answer button can take over is the call the answering machine is holding — and taking it that way ends the message at that moment.

docs.title: The certificate step, once
docs.text:
The audio stream arrives on its own port, and a browser will not accept a self-signed certificate silently on a port it has not seen before. So the page shows one button:

Open the audio address (one time)

Press it, accept the browser's warning, close that tab. The browser then remembers the router's certificate for the audio port and the step stays out of the way forever after. Until you do it, the page says so plainly rather than letting you press Use this computer's microphone and wonder why nothing happens.

docs.title: What the audio path is
docs.text:
How the browser's voice reaches the line

One HTTP request becomes a WebSocket on the router's LAN address, port 7443 by default (web_port, web_iface), carrying this daemon's own frames: twelve header bytes — marker, version, type, sequence number, timestamp — followed by 160 samples of 16-bit linear audio in network byte order, which is 20 ms at 8 kHz. At 16 kHz the same path carries two time samples per frame, packed the way the kernel reads them, so a wideband call is not stretched.

Admission is a token minted by the daemon for the call revision the page is looking at: single use, valid thirty seconds, sent in the first frame of the encrypted stream — never in a URL, never in a log, never in a form field. A refused page is told which fixed reason applied: refused-busy, refused-nocall, refused-revision, refused-mode, refused-rate, refused-port, refused-object, dropped-slow.

The stream is TLS on the router's own HTTPS certificate pair, which is /etc/uhttpd.crt and /etc/uhttpd.key unless you point it elsewhere.

Why this is not WebRTC. Three reasons, and they are all properties of this router rather than preferences: the audio has to land sample-exactly inside the kernel's audio bridge and the recording mirror, which a jitter buffer will not do; the allowed library set for this code stops short of ICE, SRTP and Opus; and the peer is always on your own LAN, where there is no NAT to traverse, no jitter to absorb and no codec negotiation to lose. A LAN stream that is 20 ms late is broken, not adaptively degraded.

docs.title: What you hear from the page
docs.text:
• your own ring: a 1 kHz double burst every four seconds while a call rings, started only after you have interacted with the page, because a browser refuses sound until then;
  • progress tones from the line itself, in the call audio;
  • nothing at all if the audio session is not open — a call can be up with the page showing its state and no sound, which is the Stop audio state, not a fault.

docs.title: When the page's phone misbehaves
docs.text: symptom what it means Use this computer's microphone does nothing the browser refused the microphone, or the page is not over HTTPS The button is there but audio never starts the certificate step has not been done in this browser. Press Open the audio address (one time) You dial and the call sets up, but you hear nothing the audio session is not open, or it was stopped. The meters being flat both ways is the tell You hear the caller and they cannot hear you the microphone is muted, or the browser revoked it mid-call Answer is greyed out while a call rings the handset is already off hook, or another front end holds the answer. That is the ownership rule, not a bug The page says the phone side is not running the daemon is down. The card offers the Health tab, where you can start it A call the page held is not taken by lifting the handset correct: a lift gets the recall dial tone, and the page's held call stays the page's

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
Can I make phone calls without an analog handset on the AW1000?

Yes. With nothing in the RJ11 socket the AWvoice page is the telephone: dial from its keypad, answer with its Answer button, hang up, mute, and send DTMF. A soft phone on your own network is a third option once the SIP switch is on.

Does the browser phone use WebRTC?

No. It uses an encrypted WebSocket on the LAN carrying this daemon's own 20 ms audio frames, admitted by a single-use token. The reason is that the audio has to be placed sample-exactly into the kernel bridge and the recording mirror, and a LAN peer needs none of what WebRTC exists for.

Why does my browser ask for a certificate warning just for audio?

The audio stream is a second port with the router's own self-signed certificate. Accepting it once, through the page's Open the audio address button, is the whole setup.

Can two people use the phone at once — the handset and the page?

One of them owns the audio at a time. Lifting the handset during a page call carries the call on at the phone and stops the page's microphone and speaker.

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
Does CleanWRT reboot the router when 5G drops?

Not as shipped. OpenWrt's Watchcat is the tool that would, and its package default is exactly that rule; this image installs Watchcat with no rule configured, so nothing reboots until you write one.

How do I collect a diagnostic report from the router?

cw-diag full. It redacts SIM identifiers, public addresses and Wi-Fi keys, which is what makes it safe to attach to a report.

Can I block ads on the whole network?

Yes, with Adblock or AdGuard Home — one of them, not both. Both are installed; both are off. See apps with their own web interface.

docs.title: Multi-WAN failover
docs.text:
Add a second internet connection and let the router switch to it if 5G drops or hits a cap.

mwan3 is not in the image

The 5G modem already reconnects by itself, so mwan3 is only needed to switch to a different connection. Install it when you need it:

apk add mwan3 luci-app-mwan3

docs.title: 1. Add the backup connection
docs.text:
Backup How Phone USB tether plug the phone in and turn on USB tethering; it appears as a network device (the rndis / ipheth driver loads automatically) USB modem or USB Ethernet adapter plug it in; usb-modeswitch turns dongles into modem mode

Add it under Network → Interfaces (DHCP).

docs.title: 2. Enable mwan3
docs.text:
/etc/init.d/mwan3 enable && /etc/init.d/mwan3 start

Configure members and policies in Network → Load Balancing. Point the primary at the modem interface (4_1) and the backup at your second connection.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Can the Arcadyan AW1000 fail over to another connection when 5G drops?

Yes, with mwan3. Add a phone USB tether, a USB modem or a USB Ethernet adapter as a second interface, then set the 5G modem as the primary member and the other as the backup.

Is mwan3 included in CleanWRT?

No. The 5G modem already reconnects by itself, so mwan3 is only needed to switch to a different connection. Install it with apk add mwan3 luci-app-mwan3.

Is mwan3 included in CleanWRT?

No. The image ships the drivers a second connection needs and leaves the policy router to you: apk add mwan3 luci-app-mwan3.

Can the AW1000 use a phone on USB tethering as a backup WAN?

Yes. The RNDIS and iPhone tethering drivers are in the image; add the interface, then let mwan3 decide when to use it.

docs.title: Remote access
docs.text:
5G gives you a CGNAT address, so port forwarding does not work. To reach the router or your LAN from outside, pick one of these. All of them ship disabled; enable only what you use.

Set a root password first

See Security. A tunnel to a router with no password is an open door.

docs.title: Tailscale
docs.text:
A mesh VPN, and the easiest option.

/etc/init.d/tailscale enable && /etc/init.d/tailscale start
tailscale up        # prints a login URL; open it to authenticate

The LuCI page is Services → Tailscale.

docs.title: Cloudflare Tunnel
docs.text:
Exposes a service through your Cloudflare account, with no public IP needed.

Services → Cloudflare Zero Trust Tunnel → Configuration: paste your tunnel token and enable.

A red cloudflared error is normal until you configure it

Until you set it up on the Configuration tab, the Tunnels and Log tabs show a red cloudflared error (config.yml was empty or no origin certificate). That is expected for an unconfigured tunnel, not a fault. Configure the token first.

docs.title: WireGuard
docs.text: You can also run your own WireGuard server on the router. See VPN and proxies.

docs.title: Which one?
docs.text: You want Use to reach the whole LAN from your devices with little setup Tailscale to publish one web service under your own domain Cloudflare Tunnel a classic VPN you control end to end (needs a public endpoint somewhere) WireGuard

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
How can I reach my router behind 5G CGNAT?

5G gives you a carrier-grade NAT address, so port forwarding does not work. Use Tailscale, a Cloudflare Tunnel or a WireGuard server you run yourself. All of them ship disabled.

Should I use Tailscale or Cloudflare Tunnel on the AW1000?

Tailscale is the easiest way to reach the whole LAN from your own devices. A Cloudflare Tunnel is better for publishing one web service under your own domain.

Why does cloudflared show a red error?

That is expected until you configure the tunnel token on the Configuration tab. It is not a fault.

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
How can I reach my router behind 5G CGNAT?

Outbound-first: Tailscale or a Cloudflare Tunnel. Both connect out, neither needs a public address or a forwarded port. WireGuard is the third option when you already have a server somewhere with an address.

Should I use Tailscale or Cloudflare Tunnel on the AW1000?

Tailscale for reaching the router and the network behind it as yourself; Cloudflare Tunnel for publishing one service to other people. They solve different problems and both are installed.

Is it safe to enable SSH on this router?

Only after you set a root password. The image ships password authentication on and no password set, which is OpenWrt's first-login model and is meant for the LAN with a cable in.

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text:
CleanWRT starts the way stock OpenWrt does:

  • No root password at first. The first login happens over Ethernet, and LuCI asks you to set one.
  • Wi-Fi is on, WPA2-PSK, with the default key CleanWRT#40. Change it on the first login.
  • Every opt-in service is disabled. Nothing listens on your network until you enable it.
  • LuCI is served over HTTPS; plain HTTP only redirects to it.

See First boot for the steps.

Before you expose the router remotely

Set your root password first. Otherwise a tunnel publishes an admin interface with no password to the internet.

docs.title: Why the browser says "Not secure"
docs.text:
The admin UI uses a self-signed TLS certificate, generated on your router at first boot. Every router gets a different one and no public authority signed it, so browsers warn exactly as they do on stock OpenWrt. The connection is still encrypted. Click Advanced → Proceed.

If you own a domain, you can get a trusted certificate:

apk add acme-common luci-app-acme

Then issue a Let's Encrypt certificate with a DNS challenge (it works behind CGNAT).

docs.title: Changing the password and the Wi-Fi key later
docs.text:
• Root password: System → Administration, or passwd over SSH.
  • Wi-Fi key: Network → Wireless, edit the interface, Wireless Security.

No re-flash is needed.

docs.text: For a security problem, please open a private report from the repository's Security tab (Report a vulnerability) if it is enabled, or open an issue that does not include exploit details and ask for a private channel.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Why does my browser say the OpenWrt router connection is not secure?

LuCI uses a self-signed certificate that your router creates at first boot. The connection is still encrypted, but no public authority signed the certificate. Click Advanced → Proceed, or install a trusted certificate with ACME if you own a domain.

What are the default passwords on CleanWRT?

There is no root password at first. The first login happens over Ethernet and LuCI asks you to set one. Wi-Fi is WPA2-PSK with the default key CleanWRT#40. Change both on the first login.

How do I get a trusted HTTPS certificate on the router?

Install acme-common and luci-app-acme, then issue a Let's Encrypt certificate with a DNS challenge. That works behind CGNAT because it needs no inbound connection.

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
Is the AW1000 safe with CleanWRT on a 5G connection?

It is a router behind carrier NAT with nothing forwarded in, and this image opens no inbound service beyond the LAN-side admin interface and the local provisioning listener. What makes it unsafe is the same thing that makes any router unsafe: no root password, and the default Wi-Fi key still in place.

docs.title: USB storage and NAS
docs.text: Plug in a USB drive and it auto-mounts under /mnt (ext4, FAT, exFAT and NTFS). Manage mounts in System → Mount Points.

docs.title: Prepare a drive in the browser
docs.text:
Services → Disk Manager creates partition tables (GPT or MBR), partitions and formats (ext4, FAT32, exFAT, NTFS, btrfs), and shows disk health (SMART, including USB-NVMe enclosures).

Mounts made in Disk Manager are live only

Set the boot-time mount in System → Mount Points afterwards so the drive is there after every reboot. The smartd daemon ships disabled; the UI only uses the smartctl command.

docs.title: NAS services (all opt-in)
docs.text:
Everything below ships installed but disabled and is pointed at the USB drive. Nothing listens on the LAN until you enable it. Set credentials before you enable each service.

Service Where Notes Network file share (SMB) Network → Filesystem Share serves all of /mnt as \\192.168.1.1\USB; guest access is off Torrents (qBittorrent) Services → qBittorrent web UI on :8080; downloads go to /mnt/download Folder sync (Syncthing) Services → Syncthing web UI on :8384 Media server (miniDLNA) Services → miniDLNA DLNA on the LAN only, port 8200 Printer share (p910nd) Services → p910nd raw port 9100 and mDNS Web file manager Tools → File Manager browse, edit, upload, delete, hex editor Drive spin-down Tools → HDD Idle for USB hard disks

More download clients are available from the official repositories:

apk add transmission-daemon transmission-web luci-app-transmission
apk add aria2 luci-app-aria2

Plug a drive in before you download

Downloads default to the first USB drive (/mnt/sda1). With no drive attached they would fill the router's small internal flash. Do not start downloads without a drive.

docs.title: Streaming to a TV or phone (DLNA)
docs.text:
1. Plug in a drive with media.
  2. Enable Services → miniDLNA; it scans /mnt.
  3. Smart TVs (Samsung, LG, Sony), VLC, Kodi, phone apps and a PS4/Xbox see the server on the LAN.

For a very large library, point the database directory at the drive (miniDLNA → Advanced), so it does not re-scan on every reboot.

PlayStation 5

The PS5 has no built-in DLNA player. Use an app such as Plex on it.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Can I use a USB drive as a NAS on the Arcadyan AW1000?

Yes. A drive auto-mounts under /mnt (ext4, FAT, exFAT and NTFS), and you can share it with SMB, DLNA, Syncthing and qBittorrent. All of these ship installed but disabled, so set credentials before you enable them.

Can the AW1000 stream media to a smart TV?

Yes. Enable miniDLNA with a drive of media attached. Smart TVs, VLC, Kodi and phone apps on the LAN will see the server. A PlayStation 5 has no built-in DLNA player, so use an app such as Plex there.

Why should I plug a drive in before downloading?

Downloads default to the first USB drive. With no drive attached they would fill the router's small internal flash.

Can I use a USB drive as a NAS on the Arcadyan AW1000?

Yes, and it is the only place this router has room. Samba serves /mnt as one writable share with guest access off, so it is private until you add users.

Can the AW1000 stream media to a smart TV?

docs.title: VPN and proxies
docs.text: All of these ship installed and disabled. They need your servers, keys or configuration.

docs.title: WireGuard
docs.text:
WireGuard is fully installed (kernel module, wg tools and LuCI protocol support) but has no interfaces configured. An empty Status page is normal until you create one.

Create a tunnel: Network → Interfaces → Add new interface, name it (for example wg0), protocol WireGuard VPN, Create interface. In the interface's Configuration tab set the private key and the peers (a peer is an endpoint plus allowed IPs).

Command line alternative:

wg genkey | tee privatekey | wg pubkey > publickey

then configure with wg set.

docs.title: OpenVPN
docs.text: VPN → OpenVPN. The service needs your .ovpn configuration, so it ships disabled. Enable it per configuration.

docs.title: Proxies and bypass tools
docs.text:
App Where Cores Passwall 2 Services → PassWall 2 Xray, Sing-box, Hysteria and more Passwall Services → PassWall the same cores HomeProxy Services → HomeProxy sing-box

Add a node (server), pick the matching core, set the routing mode and enable. dnsmasq-full and chinadns-ng are already wired in.

Use one proxy suite at a time

Running more than one proxy suite on the same router makes firewall and DNS rules fight. Enable the one you want.

IPv6: if you send traffic through Passwall 2, enable IPv6 TProxy in its forwarding settings. Passwall 1 hides IPv6 answers for proxied names by default.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Does CleanWRT include WireGuard and OpenVPN?

Yes. WireGuard is fully installed with no interfaces configured, and OpenVPN needs your own .ovpn configuration. Both ship disabled.

Can I run Passwall and HomeProxy at the same time?

It is better not to. Several proxy suites on one router make firewall and DNS rules fight, so enable the one you want.

Why do I need IPv6 TProxy in Passwall 2?

Without it, devices can reach IPv6 sites directly, outside the proxy. Enable it in the forwarding settings when you proxy traffic through Passwall 2.

docs.title: Questions people ask
docs.text:
Does CleanWRT include WireGuard and OpenVPN?

Yes. WireGuard is a kernel module plus tools and a LuCI page; OpenVPN is installed with its own page and needs your configuration file. Neither is configured out of the box.

Can I run Passwall and HomeProxy at the same time?

You can install both, but only one should be enabled: they both install transparent-proxy rules and the second one silently changes where the first one's traffic goes.

Why do I need IPv6 TProxy in Passwall 2?

Because the 5G connection is dual-stack when your carrier offers IPv6, and a proxy that only captures IPv4 leaves IPv6 traffic going out directly.

docs.title: Apps with their own web interface
docs.text: Some apps are configured in their own dashboard, opened in the browser, and not inside LuCI. The three below are installed with the firmware. The examples assume the router is at 192.168.1.1.

docs.title: Start and stop an app
docs.text:
Every app has an Enable box on its LuCI page (Services → the app's name). Tick it and press Save & Apply to start; untick it and press Save & Apply to stop. One switch, the same everywhere.

Advanced: System → Startup lists services with Start and Stop buttons. They act only for the current session. The Enable box is what decides whether the app runs after a reboot.

docs.title: Syncthing: folder sync
docs.text:
Keeps folders in step between your phone, your PC and a drive on the router.

  1. Services → Syncthing, tick Enable, Save & Apply.
  2. Open the dashboard: http://192.168.1.1:8384.
  3. First thing to do: Actions → Settings → GUI, set a user name and password. Until then anyone on your network can open the dashboard.
  4. Add your other devices (Add Remote Device) and choose the folders to share.

To keep the dashboard private to the router itself, set the Dashboard address on the LuCI page to http://127.0.0.1:8384.

docs.title: AdGuard Home: DNS filtering
docs.text:
Blocks ads and trackers for every device and shows what each device looks up.

  1. Services → AdGuard Home, tick Enable, Save & Apply.
  2. The first time, the setup wizard is at http://192.168.1.1:3000.
  3. In the wizard choose a dashboard port other than 80 or 443 (LuCI uses those) and a DNS port other than 53, unless you move the router's own DNS (dnsmasq).
  4. Finish the wizard and open the dashboard at the address you chose.

Adblock does a similar job. Use one of them, not both.

docs.title: qBittorrent: download client
docs.text:
Downloads to a USB drive attached to the router, controlled from a web page.

  1. Services → qBittorrent, tick Enable, Save & Apply.
  2. Open http://192.168.1.1:8080.
  3. The user is admin. There is no shared default password: until you set your own, qBittorrent makes a temporary one every time it starts and prints it to the log. Read it with logread -e qbittorrent (System → Logs).
  4. Set your own: Tools → Options → Web UI → Authentication.

The default download folder is on the USB drive (/mnt); attach and mount it first.

OpenWrt keeps its configuration in UCI files under /etc/config/, one file per package, and LuCI writes the same files the shell does. This is the index of the options this image cares about.

With no type, the whole log recordings none {recordings: [{name, bytes, rate, channels, seconds}]} recording_get name, offset {name, total, offset, b64, more} — 24 KiB of raw audio per reply recording_delete name {ok, removed} messages none as the recordings, with ts added message_get, message_delete as the recording pair as the recording pair greeting_get offset {total, offset, b64, more}. There is no name: one fixed file greeting_begin none opens a staged write greeting_put offset, b64 up to 16 KiB of plain bytes per call greeting_commit polish 1 asks for the trim-and-tone treatment. Waits for a quiet line and refuses with -EBUSY if it cannot get one greeting_abort none discards the staged file

Every file name is checked before it is touched

recording_get, recording_delete, message_get and message_delete accept only a name of the exact form <epoch>-<call id>.wav, 7 to 64 characters. Anything else is refused before the filesystem is consulted, which is what makes the page's delete buttons safe to expose.

docs.title: Object qmodem_voip
docs.text:
This is the front end a network phone is carried through. It is published only while the SIP side is on, the guards leave the line free, and no other program already holds the name.

method what you pass notes status nothing state, origin (always cellular), endpoint, number_present, caller_id_withheld, remote_number, duration, held, waiting, revision, restart_epoch, sequence, drop_count, reconcile_pending, answer_owner, media_engine, and the two media frame counters capabilities none media: "qmsk", sample_rate: 8000, frame_ms: 20, frame_samples: 160, wideband: 0, calls: 1, endpoints: ["lan_sip", "cellular", "browser"] originate endpoint, number, origin, username the endpoint must be one of the three words, or the refusal is refused-mode answer none takes over a call the answering machine holds. The reply waits up to 6 seconds for the call to list as active, and answers no-answer if it never does reject, hangup none a hang-up with nothing to end is accepted send_dtmf digit first character only issue_socket_session call_revision returns session_id. Eight live bindings at once

flash is not on this object — it is the browser page's own key.

docs.title: First-boot defaults
docs.text:
OpenWrt runs the scripts in /etc/uci-defaults/ in name order on a clean boot. A script that exits 0 is deleted, so it runs once; one that exits non-zero stays and is retried at the next boot. This page is the complete list of what this image writes, and what it deliberately does not touch.

Everything here is in the repository under files/etc/uci-defaults/, so a router that has already booted can be checked against the source.

These scripts run before you log in

The first boot is when the defaults below are written. A setting you change afterwards is not overwritten by a later sysupgrade that keeps settings — with the two exceptions noted in their rows.

docs.title: The image's own scripts
docs.text: script what it writes when it leaves things alone 45-cw-strip-stock-leds removes the LuCI menu node admin/system/leds from luci-mod-system.json and deletes the stock view/system/leds.js, then clears the LuCI caches. The LED Management daemon owns those lamps it writes the menu file back only if the System menu is still intact and the LEDs node really went; the led sections in /etc/config/system are not removed, nor the WAN port lamp 46-cw-uhttpd-https uhttpd.main.redirect_https='1', so plain HTTP becomes HTTPS exits quietly if /etc/config/uhttpd is missing 47-cw-awvoice-at-port deletes the ubus-at-daemon port section, which frees /dev/ttyUSB2 for the phone port. QModem keeps ttyUSB3 only if that config file exists. To undo: re-add the port section with its at_port set to /dev/ttyUSB2 48-cw-strip-asu-ui removes every Attended Sysupgrade menu node — the package keys its pages as admin/system/attendedsysupgrade/overview and …/configuration, so the parent goes with them — and deletes their views, turns the Status page's newer-version check on (attendedsysupgrade.client.login_check_for_upgrades='1') — those views are the only switch that ever turned it on, so the notice is on out of the box and its own button is the way off — then clears the caches. attendedsysupgrade-common stays it writes the menu back unless no key carries that path any more, and skips the option where the config has no client section. See releases for what the notice does 49-cw-awvoice-provision-port adds a second uhttpd instance, uhttpd.awvoice_provision: listen_http='0.0.0.0:8080', home='/www/awvoice-provision', redirect_https='0', no_dirlists='1', rfc1918_filter='1', and creates that directory. This is the plain-HTTP listener a scanned provisioning code points a soft phone at exits if /etc/config/uhttpd is missing. To undo: delete the section, remove the directory, restart uhttpd 50-cw-footstrap-look writes the image's look into /etc/config/footstrap — 27 options: layout='top', darkmode='dark', palette='footstrap', wallpaper='file', material='frosted', blur='30', rounding='12', card_opacity='55', bar_opacity='55', photo_dim='15', pattern_size='440', pattern_strength='20', pattern_ink='theme', content_width='1280', density='normal', autocollapse='off', colour tints at 0, plus login_bg and pattern set to the checksums of the two files the image installs, and cw_look='rc2.1' three reasons to do nothing: the router already carries the look this script names; the current login_bg is a photo that is not one of the image's two files; or either installed file's checksum cannot be read. Your own saved look always outranks the image's. See theme 51-cw-awvoice-voipd-off stops the vendor VoIP engine qmodem_voip and takes it off the boot path, so the phone daemon can answer the front-end name itself and the network phone carries audio exits if the init script is not executable. It fails — and retries next boot — if any boot link for that engine survives other than the SIP service's own. This is the fix for a soft phone that registers and never sets up media 96-cw-apk-world-pin rewrites /etc/apk/world from the installed package database: every package that came from the LuCI feed, plus base-files, kernel and any kmod-*, is pinned to its exact version; everything else is written as a bare name and stays upgradable it runs on every boot, so the pins always match the running image. The reason is recorded in the script: one apk upgrade once replaced patched LuCI packages with stock ones 96-cw-default-theme luci.themes.Footstrap=/luci-static/footstrap and luci.main.mediaurlbase=/luci-static/footstrap, and deletes a dead marker section an older image left only if /www/luci-static/footstrap exists and the current base is empty, still the stock bootstrap, or names a directory that no longer exists. If you chose another theme, your choice stands 97-cw-adguard-enable-bridge hands off to /usr/libexec/cw-adguard-enable-bridge, which wires AdGuard Home's local upstream so the router's own DNS still resolves when the filter is enabled a non-zero exit keeps the script for a retry at the next boot 97-cw-net-tuning network.globals.packet_steering='1', spreading receive and transmit work over the four cores unconditional 98-cw-modem-fix /etc/init.d/cw-modem-fix enable, which puts the modem registration fix on the boot path unconditional. See the 5G modem 99-aw1000-defaults system.@system[0].hostname='CleanWRT', .timezone='UTC', .log_size='64'; dropbear password authentication and root password authentication on; for each radio: enabled, ssid='CleanWRT-2.4G' / 'CleanWRT-5G' / 'CleanWRT-6G' by band, encryption='psk2', key='CleanWRT#40' the Wi-Fi key is written only if no key is set yet, so a keep-settings upgrade never regenerates it. The regulatory domain is deliberately not hardcoded — it follows the network the modem registers on. The root password is left unset on purpose. psk2 rather than sae-mixed because some clients failed to associate otherwise

docs.text:

script where it comes from what it does 90-cw-led luci-app-cw-led removes from /etc/config/system every led section whose sysfs node is one the LED daemon owns (blue:5g, green:5g, red:5g, blue:signal, green:signal, red:signal, green:internet), reseeds the daemon's own global section only if it is missing, enables the service and reloads rpcd. green:power, green:wifi and the WAN lamp keep their kernel triggers 89-qmodem-sip-migrate, 90-qmodem-sip-firewall, 91-qmodem-sip-voip-off the QModem feed's SIP service, the last one added by this build's patch patches/feeds/qmodem/0009-sip-voip-default-migration.patch migrate a configuration that still pointed at the vendor engine, add the service's firewall include, and set both directions' voip_enabled to 0 only when the media socket path is the phone daemon's — which is how an upgrade from an older image ends up with working audio 30_luci-theme-argon Argon, with one line removed by patches/packages/luci-theme-argon/0001-argon-registers-itself-and-leaves-the-default.patch registers the theme but no longer makes it the default design. docs.title: What the image ships as configuration
docs.text:
The scripts above change things; these files are simply there from the start. Full option lists are in UCI options.

file state on a new router adblock adb_enabled='0'. Off until you tick the checkbox on its page fstab USB drives are auto-mounted under /mnt; no anonymous swap, no filesystem check at boot irqbalance enabled minidlna enabled='0'; when on, port 8200 on the LAN, media from /mnt, name CleanWRT p910nd enabled='0'; when on, /dev/usb/lp0 with an mDNS advertisement labelled CleanWRT USB printer qmodem_ttl enabled, TTL of forwarded packets rewritten to 64 samba4 the daemon starts, with one share (USB → /mnt, writable) and guest_ok='no', so nothing is reachable until you add users syncthing enabled='0'; when on, its own interface on 0.0.0.0:8384 and its config in /etc/syncthing watchcat comment lines only, no sections. The package default is an active "ping, reboot after 6 failures" rule; this file replaces it so the router never reboots itself unless you add a rule cw-led, awvoice, footstrap, qmodem_sip shipped by their own packages, not here, so an upgrade keeps what you changed

docs.title: Reading it on your router
docs.text:
Nothing here is hidden. On a flashed router:

ls /etc/uci-defaults/          # what is still waiting to run
logread -e cw-firstboot        # what the image's own scripts said
uci show footstrap             # the look the image applied
uci show awvoice               # the line, the network side, the quiet-hours windows

A script that already ran is gone from that directory, which is why the log and the config — not the leftovers — are the evidence of what happened.
